channel.title: Cadence Evidence — PT Research Signal
channel.description: Daily curated physical therapy & rehab research for clinicians. AI-scored signal from 56 sources.

item.title: Video-based education is non-inferior to in-person education in patients undergoing arthroscopic partial meniscectomy: a non-inferiority randomized controlled trial | Archives of Physiotherapy
item.description: A non-inferiority RCT (n=166) found that preoperative video-based education was non-inferior to postoperative in-person education for pain-related self-efficacy (PSEQ MD: -0.6 at T1; -0.5 at T2) and led to better fear of movement scores (TSK) in patients undergoing arthroscopic partial meniscectomy.
item.author: Arch Physiother

item.title: Physical Therapy Management of Fall Risk in Community-Dwelling Older Adults (CPG+)
item.description: APTA Geriatrics has published an updated Clinical Practice Guideline (CPG+) for the physical therapy management of fall risk in community-dwelling adults aged 65 and over, replacing the 2015 version and including a clinical reasoning algorithm.
item.author: APTA

item.title: The effect of multimodal sensory therapy in consciousness improvement in patients with acquired brain injury: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
item.description: A systematic review and meta-analysis (18 studies, 884 participants) found that multimodal sensory therapy significantly improved consciousness levels (SMD, 1.48; 95% CI, 1.04-1.92) and increased the odds of coma emergence (OR, 9.85; 95% CI, 3.86-25.01) in adults with acquired brain injury-related disorders of consciousness.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Exercise-only interventions and exercise-based multidomain lifestyle interventions to promote cognitive function in older adults without dementia: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
item.description: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 227 studies found that exercise-only interventions significantly improved executive functions, memory, and processing speed in older adults without dementia compared to control. Exercise-plus interventions (exercise combined with other lifestyle factors) were significantly better than control for memory, and better than exercise-only for executive functions and processing speed, but not memory.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: The Effects of Exergames on Fundamental Movement Skills in Childhood: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis
item.description: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 12 studies (17 comparisons) concluded that low-barrier exergames are as effective as traditional activities for fundamental movement skill adaptation in children. The variability in effects was explained by coaching and activity structure, rather than exergame status itself.
item.author: Sports Med - Open

item.title: Fatigue-related neuromuscular outcomes following ACL reconstruction: a systematic review and meta-analysis
item.description: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 17 studies (n=477) found that individuals with ACLR demonstrated lower post-fatigue quadriceps CAR (SMD: -0.69, p < 0.001) and muscle activation patterns (SMD: -0.62, p < 0.001) compared to healthy controls, with moderate certainty of evidence.
item.author: BMC Sports Sci Med Rehabil

item.title: Motor-Based Interventions in Children with Developmental Coordination Disorder: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis of Randomised Controlled Trials - Sports Medicine - Open
item.description: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 32 RCTs found that motor-based interventions (MBI) significantly improved overall motor skills (g=1.00), balance (g=0.57), cognitive (g=1.53), and activity performance (g=0.71) in children with DCD. Task-oriented training showed particular effectiveness, but MBI did not significantly improve psychosocial factors or participation levels.
item.author: Sports Med - Open

item.title: Effect of Sequential Electroacupuncture Combined With Augmented Reality Gait Training on Walking Function and Neuromuscular Control in Subacute Stroke: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
item.description: A single-blind RCT (n=40) in subacute stroke patients found that sequential electroacupuncture combined with augmented reality gait training significantly improved gait speed (Wald χ²=6.509, P=0.011), stride length, gait symmetry, motor function, and balance compared to AR alone after 4 weeks.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Physical Exercise Reduces Fall-Related Outcomes Among People With Stroke: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
item.description: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 18 RCTs (1536 participants) found that physical exercise significantly reduced the number of falls by 39% (IRR = 0.61, 95% CI = [0.47, 0.78]) in people with stroke, with balance and cognitively integrated training being most effective, especially for those in the chronic stage with mild-moderate disability.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Leader and Follower Roles in Adapted Tango Reveal Complementary Neural Routes to Motor Improvement in Parkinson's Disease
item.description: An RCT randomized people with mild-to-moderate Parkinson's Disease (PD) to 12 weeks of adapted tango as Leaders, Followers, or a Control. Both dance groups showed significant clinical improvement, including reduced overall disease severity and motor impairment, with Leaders showing network stability and Followers increased sensorimotor/caudate-motor connectivity, suggesting complementary neural routes to motor improvement.
item.author: medRxiv

item.title: Short-Term Effects of Radial Extracorporeal Shock Wave Therapy in Addition to Physiotherapy on Spasticity, Walking Performance, and Quality of Life in Chronic Stroke: A Sham-Controlled Randomized Trial.
item.description: Adding 4 weeks of radial extracorporeal shock wave therapy to physiotherapy significantly improved spasticity (-0.56 MAS, 95% CI -0.77 to -0.35), walking performance (-1.41 s 10MWT), motor function, and quality of life in chronic stroke patients, with no adverse events.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Single-bundle versus double-bundle reconstruction in anterior cruciate ligament: a meta-analysis
item.description: A meta-analysis of 41 RCTs (n=3,568) found that DB ACL reconstruction showed statistically higher rates of negative pivot-shift test (short-term OR=0.62, p<0.001; long-term OR=0.37, p=0.007) and higher long-term Lysholm scores (MD=-1.32, p=0.004) compared to SB, but no clinically meaningful superiority for most patients.
item.author: BMC Musculoskelet Disord

item.title: Is therapeutic exercise as a standalone intervention effective in reducing kinesiophobia in adults with nonspecific chronic low back pain? A systematic review and meta-analysis with meta-regression
item.description: A systematic review and meta-analysis of eight RCTs (854 participants) found that standalone therapeutic exercise significantly reduced kinesiophobia in adults with nonspecific chronic low back pain compared to passive controls and usual care (MD = −5.38; 95% CI −7.63 to −3.13; SMD = −1.03), exceeding the minimal clinically important difference, despite low certainty of evidence and high heterogeneity.
item.author: Eur Spine J

item.title: Approach to sarcopenia in older adults: a systematic review of dietary and exercise interventions in the primary care setting
item.description: A systematic review of six RCTs (444 experimental, 226 control participants) found that combined dietary and exercise interventions, particularly physical exercise paired with nutritional supplementation, demonstrated notable improvements in muscle strength, physical function, and body composition in older adults with sarcopenia in primary care settings.
item.author: BMC Geriatrics

item.title: Multimodal high-intensity interval training elicits greater improvements in aerobic capacity and sprint performance versus small-sided games and drill-based HIIT in adolescent basketball players: a randomized controlled trial
item.description: A randomized controlled trial (n=36) found that multimodal high-intensity interval training (M-HIIT) led to greater improvements in estimated VO₂max (+10.9%, d=2.33) and 20-m sprint time (-5.1%, d=-1.92) compared to small-sided games (SSG) and drill-based HIIT (DB-HIIT) in adolescent basketball players.
item.author: BMC Sports Sci Med Rehabil

item.title: REmotely monitored, Mobile health-supported Multidomain Rehabilitation with High Intensity Interval Training for COVID-19 (REMM-HIIT-CoV): Trial Design and Rationale.
item.description: The REMM-HIIT-CoV trial is a multicenter, single-blinded RCT (N=140) evaluating a 12-week remotely delivered, mobile health-supported multidomain rehabilitation program with high-intensity interval training for post-hospitalized COVID-19 survivors, primarily assessing 6-minute walk distance at 3 months.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Age, resilience, social support, and health literacy as predictors of functional ability in people with spinal cord injury: a 6-month follow-up study.
item.description: A 6-month follow-up study of 367 inpatients with traumatic SCI found that younger age (β = -0.02; p = 0.028), higher resilience (β = 0.22; p < 0.001), and higher health literacy (β = 0.32; p = 0.001) were independent predictors of greater functional ability, though overall improvement was modest (MBI 43.50 to 46.81).
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Perceptions and Experiences of Returning to Sport Following Myocardial Infarction: A Qualitative Study.
item.description: This qualitative study explored perceptions and experiences of returning to sport after a myocardial infarction, identifying themes like reconciling active identity with new reality, feeling vulnerable, needing strong support, and navigating their own path, highlighting significant psychosocial challenges alongside high motivation.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Real-time continuous assessment of fatigue from surface electromyography with deep learning for training load regulation in elite cyclists
item.description: A deep learning model combining CNN, Bi-LSTM, and channel attention mechanisms was developed to continuously estimate fatigue from raw sEMG signals during high-intensity cycling in 14 elite cyclists. The model achieved a mean absolute error of 0.048 ± 0.019 and a Pearson correlation of 0.822 ± 0.123, showing superior accuracy over baseline models.
item.author: BMC Sports Sci Med Rehabil

item.title: Neurophysiological and neuromuscular responses associated with the repeated bout effect following eccentric exercise in healthy adults: a systematic review and meta-analysis
item.description: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 12 studies found that peripheral contractile outcomes showed the most consistent recovery-compatible pattern after repeated eccentric exercise bouts. Evidence concerning central activation and motor-unit behavior was limited or inconsistent, leaving the contribution of neural changes to the repeated bout effect unresolved.
item.author: Eur J Appl Physiol
